new.md:
Creates a new toggle button.

A widget should be packed into the button, as in [`Button.new()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#constructor:new).

new_with_label.brief: Creates a new toggle button with a text label.
new_with_label.md: Creates a new toggle button with a text label.

new_with_mnemonic.brief: Creates a new `GtkToggleButton` containing a label.
new_with_mnemonic.md:
Creates a new `GtkToggleButton` containing a label.

The label will be created using [`Label.new_with_mnemonic()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Label#constructor:new_with_mnemonic),
so underscores in `label` indicate the mnemonic for the button.

doc.brief: Shows a button which remains “pressed-in” when clicked.

get_active.brief: Queries a `GtkToggleButton` and returns its current state.
get_active.md:
Queries a `GtkToggleButton` and returns its current state.

Returns `TRUE` if the toggle button is pressed in and `FALSE`
if it is raised.

set_active.brief: Sets the status of the toggle button.
set_active.md:
Sets the status of the toggle button.

Set to `TRUE` if you want the `GtkToggleButton` to be “pressed in”,
and `FALSE` to raise it.

If the status of the button changes, this action causes the
[`ToggleButton::toggled`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ToggleButton#event:toggled) signal to be emitted.

set_group.md:
Adds `self` to the group of `group`.

In a group of multiple toggle buttons, only one button can be active
at a time.

Setting up groups in a cycle leads to undefined behavior.

Note that the same effect can be achieved via the [`Actionable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Actionable)
API, by using the same action with parameter type and state type 's'
for all buttons in the group, and giving each button its own target
value.

toggled.deprecated_md: There is no good reason for an application ever to call this function.
